warnings: The load generator and the server under test share one machine. Their CPU use competes, so absolute numbers are pessimistic compared with a dedicated client. Use results to compare runs on the same machine.

resources.note: CPU is the server process only, as a percentage of one core. The load generator runs in a separate process on the same machine, so it competes for the same CPU.

bottlenecks.title: Throughput stopped scaling at "step 2"
bottlenecks.detail: Users grew 79% from "step 1" to "step 2" but throughput grew only 24% while p95 rose 65%. The system is close to its capacity around 43 users.

bottlenecks.title: Throughput stopped scaling at "step 3"
bottlenecks.detail: Users grew 47% from "step 2" to "step 3" but throughput grew only -15% while p95 rose 91%. The system is close to its capacity around 63 users.

bottlenecks.title: Throughput stopped scaling at "step 5"
bottlenecks.detail: Users grew 23% from "step 4" to "step 5" but throughput grew only -8% while p95 rose 54%. The system is close to its capacity around 101 users.

bottlenecks.title: Server process CPU was saturated
bottlenecks.detail: CPU of the server process was at or above 85% of one core for 33 of 116 seconds. Node.js handles requests on one thread, so this is a likely bottleneck.

bottlenecks.title: Event-loop delay was high
bottlenecks.detail: The event loop was delayed up to 2146.44 ms (p95 in a one-second window). Requests queue behind synchronous work such as password hashing, large JSON or database calls.

reasons: Some metrics moved noticeably but not beyond their limits, or the change is within the runs' own variation.

warnings.message: Both runs are the same code version: any difference is noise, not a regression.

limitations: Latency percentiles are exact over every request in each run, but they include warm-up and ramp periods, and the load generator shares the machine with the server for local runs.

findings.subject: step 4
findings.note: Only the slowest requests changed; the median and average did not. That looks like a few outliers, not a shift. Repeat the run to confirm.
